newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts welcome ABN AMRO strategic buy.
newsitem.headline: Analysts welcome ABN AMRO strategic buy.

text.p: Dutch-based analysts applauded ABN AMROs' acquisition of a near 90 percent stake in Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB), saying that although it was a relatively small acquisition, it was a good strategic move.
The biggest Dutch bank earlier said it had been chosen by the Hunagrian authorities to buy the stake for $89.23 million.
"It's a good move -- a spring-board to eastern Europe," said NIBStrating analyst Tom Muller.
Others commented that it was a strategic step for ABN AMRO to have a local presence in eastern Europe as many of its global corporate clients were expanding there.
"It fits ABN's strategy to expand worldwide, as it wants to be a global player," said Harry Luchtenveld of Generale Bank.
"It's a growth market and ABN AMRO has to be there," added Rutger Terluin at Amstgeld. "It's very good to have local expertise -- knowledge of local rules and legislation," he said.
Analysts said ABN AMRO had funds to buy more banks globally, especially since it is selling its MeesPierson merchant bank unit to Fortis -- a deal worth an estimated 2.0 to 2.5 billion guilders.
"I foresee a big acquisition in the not-too-distant future," said Muller, predicting some activity in the United States.
ABN AMRO, Europe's fifth largest bank with total assets of $384.3 billion, started business in Hungary in 1990, but the MHB will give it access to a network of 70 branches across the country.
"They want to be in the top ten in the world," Muller said.
